correctness.rationale: Uniform unordered-pair stationary law and Hamming distance J give pi_j=w_j/N, upward radial rate a_j=2(d-j)(q-1), downward b_j=2j (j>=2), and total successful hop rate lambda_j=2d(q-1)-2*1[j=1], INCLUDING within-J transitions at q>2. First two derivatives of tilted full generator yield variance-rate mu+2<lambda-mu,(-Q)^(-1)(lambda-mu)> for the reversible system, reducible to a radial Poisson equation. Summation over j gives flux pi_j*a_j*(g_{j+1}-g_j)=-pi_1*sum_{h>j}pi_h and exact positive energy, yielding formula. First tail term dominates fixed-q asymptotic: higher terms split at binomial mode with uniform fixed-q remainder bounds. Full pair-state Q built independently and solved with exact rational linear algebra for (q,d)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2): mu,F precisely (8/3,10/9),(36/7,52/49),(7,29/28). This is not an assertion of full-process Poisson convergence.

value.rationale: This evaluates an exact natural fluctuation invariant for the canonical two-particle exclusion model on every q-ary Hamming graph, proving positive excess noise and an unexpectedly sharp dimension correction. It distinguishes counted same-distance hops and compares the one-factor Poisson boundary, a motivated physical question beyond mere simulation.

final_claim: For stationary two-particle symmetric exclusion on H(d,q), d,q>=2, all successful hops counted, mean mu=2d(q-1)(q^d-2)/(q^d-1), Fano ratio 1+2d/[N²(N-1)]*sum_{j=1}^{d-1}S_j²/[(d-j)w_j]>1 with N=q^d-1; fixed-q excess asymptotic 2/[d(q-1)q^d]. H(1,q), q>=3 is Poisson; H(1,2) has no jumps.
limitations: Exactly two indistinguishable hard-core particles, stationary symmetric rate-one jumps.
No full Poisson-process limit, varying q with d, higher cumulants, or general density.
